cards.text: Jesus is in a house with His disciples, still teaching them about the kingdom of heaven (Matt 13:36). Now He says it's like treasure hidden in a field. Friend, if I found treasure in a field, the WHOLE Dorinverse would hear me yelling about it.

cards.question: A man finds that treasure hidden in the field. What's the first thing he does with it?
After he hides the treasure again, the man goes and sells all he has. What does he buy with it?
True or false: the man in the field is gloomy about selling all he has.

cards.text: Again, Jesus says the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls. I picture this man squinting at every pearl in town like it's hiding something from him.

cards.question: The merchant finds one very precious pearl. True or false: to buy it, he sells all he has.

cards.text: Once again, Jesus paints a new picture: the kingdom of heaven is like a net cast into the sea. Fields, pearls, now fishing. Jesus is covering EVERY job in town!

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, a net gets cast into the sea. What does it catch?

cards.text: When the net is full, the men pull it ashore and sit down. I bet that job takes a while, kind of like me going over a fresh batch, cookie by cookie.

cards.question: Sitting on the shore, the men sort the ___ fish into containers and throw the ___ away.

cards.text: Then Jesus says it will be like that at the end of the age. Friend, this is where the fishing story gets serious.

cards.question: Jesus says that at the end of the age, the ___ will come and separate the wicked from the righteous.
At the end of the age, the angels separate the wicked from the righteous. Where does Jesus say they throw the wicked?

cards.text: Jesus says there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there. Then He asks His disciples, "Have you understood all these things?"

cards.question: True or false: when Jesus asks if they've understood all these things, the disciples answer yes.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them that every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner with a storeroom. A storeroom! Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer. I RESPECT a man with storage.

cards.question: Jesus says that homeowner brings out of his storeroom ___ treasures as well as ___.

cards.text: New treasures AND old ones, out of the same storeroom. Back in that drawer, nobody ever called the old stuff a treasure. So yeah, this one makes me smile.

findings.problem: Story card has three sentences: the net picture, then 'Fields, pearls, now fishing.' and 'Jesus is covering EVERY job in town!' Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Only the good fish' puts the idea of 'good fish' on screen before card 10. Card 10 asks the baker to fill in 'good' and 'bad' fish, so this card hints at its answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong word 'fresh' means nearly the same as the right word 'good' for fish being kept. 'Sort the fresh fish into containers and throw the bad away' could be argued right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Story card has four sentences: the storeroom line, 'A storeroom!', the junk drawer line, and the punchline. Story cards are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The last card repeats what card 17 already answered ('New treasures AND old ones') and adds a reflection. It tells no new part of the passage. Verse 52 is already fully covered by cards 16 and 17.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Story card has three sentences. Story cards are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'So yeah, this one makes me smile' is a mild, pleasant line, not a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
